title: Hooke's Law and Force Constant
notes: **Hooke's law:** within the elastic limit, the extension of an elastic body is directly proportional to the applied force: $F \propto x$, or $F = kx$.
**Force constant $k$:** the stiffness of the material. A larger $k$ means more force is needed for the same extension. Units: N/m.
**Elastic limit:** the maximum stress beyond which the material does not return to its original shape when the load is removed.
**Limit of proportionality:** the point beyond which $F$ is no longer proportional to $x$. The elastic limit is usually just beyond this point.
**Springs in series and parallel:** for series, $1/k_{eq} = 1/k_1 + 1/k_2$; for parallel, $k_{eq} = k_1 + k_2$. Parallel springs are stiffer; series springs are softer.
